cleanIntro: The Gold Cup National Match is a 1911 built for the target line, and two of its differences from a service 1911 change how you handle it on the bench: a PATENTED BARREL AND BUSHING fitted deliberately tight, and an ADJUSTABLE TRIGGER STOP. ⛔ The tight bushing is why Colt tells you to use the bushing wrench rather than force, and it is why the recoil spring plug is under real pressure when it comes free. ⚠ And the accuracy this pistol is bought for is exactly what a careless cleaning rod destroys — Colt says so in as many words.

steps.title: ⛔ Prove it empty — magazine out, chamber looked at
steps.action: Drop the magazine, lock the slide back and LOOK into the chamber, then put a finger in it. Colt's own strip procedure opens with this and its cleaning procedure repeats it as a CAUTION. ⚠ The magazine holds seven rounds; an eighth being absent from the magazine proves nothing about the chamber.
steps.prose: A target pistol lives on a line where it is loaded and unloaded all day. That is exactly the habit that puts a round in a chamber nobody checked.
steps.quote: The magazine has seven rounds capacity.
steps.cite: COLT GOLD CUP NATIONAL MATCH MK IV/SERIES 70 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Section 2 — Main Features, printed p.4

steps.title: Muzzle UP, resting on the butt and the grip safety
steps.action: Stand the pistol on the heel of the butt and the grip safety, muzzle pointing upward, on a bench. ⛔ That attitude is not decoration: it puts the recoil spring plug at the top where you can hold it, and it keeps the muzzle off the bench.
steps.prose: Everything that follows depends on controlling one spring. This is the grip that lets you.
steps.quote:
With muzzle pointing upward,
rest pistol on heel of butt and
"grip safety" on a table or bench.
steps.cite: COLT GOLD CUP NATIONAL MATCH MK IV/SERIES 70 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Maintenance — Stripping for Cleaning, step 2, printed p.26

steps.title: ⛔ HOLD THE PLUG — the recoil spring is under it, and the bushing is TIGHT
steps.action: Push the slide back about a quarter inch, press DOWN on the recoil spring plug just below the muzzle, and at the same time rotate the barrel bushing clockwise about a quarter turn — using the BARREL BUSHING WRENCH if you need it. ⛔ Keep pressure on the plug so the spring cannot launch it, then let plug and spring extend gradually. ⚠ This pistol's bushing is deliberately tighter than a service 1911's; that is where its accuracy comes from and why the wrench exists.
steps.prose: The one moment in a 1911 strip that puts a spring under your thumb, made stiffer here by the match fit.
steps.caution: Glasses on. Let it out slowly rather than releasing it.
steps.quote:
Push slide back about one
quarter inch, press down on recoil
spring plug (located just below
muzzle) and at same time rotate
barrel bushing clockwise about 1/4
turn, using barrel bushing wrench
steps.cite: COLT GOLD CUP NATIONAL MATCH MK IV/SERIES 70 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Maintenance — Stripping for Cleaning, step 3, printed p.26

steps.title: Plug off the spring, then cock the hammer
steps.action: Rotate the plug counterclockwise and take it off the spring. Then cock the hammer by pulling back on the hammer spur — with the pistol already proved empty. ⚠ The hammer must be back before the slide stop will come out.
steps.prose: Cocking an empty pistol you have just verified is not the same act as cocking one you have not.
steps.quote:
Rotate plug counterclockwise
and remove from spring.
steps.cite: COLT GOLD CUP NATIONAL MATCH MK IV/SERIES 70 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Maintenance — Stripping for Cleaning, step 4, printed p.26

steps.title: Slide back to the DISASSEMBLY NOTCH, then the slide stop
steps.action: Pull the slide rearward until the lug on the slide stop lines up with the DISASSEMBLY NOTCH — a different notch from the one the slide locks back on — then push the rounded end of the slide stop pin inward from the RIGHT side of the receiver and lift the slide stop out.
steps.prose: Two notches, and only one of them lets the pistol come apart. Lining up the wrong one is why the pin will not move.
steps.quote:
Pull slide to rear until lug on slide stop is opposite disassembly
notch (See Figure 9) and push rounded end of pin of slide stop
(on right of receiver) inward and through receiver to disengage
slide stop from slide.
steps.cite: COLT GOLD CUP NATIONAL MATCH MK IV/SERIES 70 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Maintenance — Stripping for Cleaning, step 6, printed p.27

steps.title: Receiver off the back, then the recoil spring and guide
steps.action: Draw the receiver rearward and off the slide. Then lift the recoil spring and its guide and pull them rearward out of the slide.
steps.prose: Rearward, both of them. Nothing on a 1911 comes out forward except the barrel.
steps.quote: Lift recoil spring and guide and pull them rearward out of slide.
steps.cite: COLT GOLD CUP NATIONAL MATCH MK IV/SERIES 70 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Maintenance — Stripping for Cleaning, step 9, printed p.27

steps.title: Bushing counterclockwise, then the barrel out the FRONT
steps.action: Turn the barrel bushing counterclockwise, push the barrel and bushing forward until the bushing is clear of the slide, and take the bushing off the barrel. Then push the LINK forward and draw the barrel out of the front of the slide.
steps.prose: The link has to be forward or the barrel will not clear. That is the whole trick of the last step.
steps.aside: Push link forward and remove barrel from front of slide.
steps.quote:
Turn barrel bushing counterclockwise, push barrel and barrel
bushing forward until bushing is clear of slide, then remove bushing
from barrel.
steps.cite: COLT GOLD CUP NATIONAL MATCH MK IV/SERIES 70 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Maintenance — Stripping for Cleaning, step 10, printed p.27

steps.title: ⛔ That is the whole strip — Colt says stop here
steps.action: Barrel, bushing, recoil spring and guide, plug, slide stop, slide and receiver. ⛔ Colt's own IMPORTANT note bars going further and routes anything deeper to Service and Repair.
steps.prose: A match pistol is fitted. Parts that are fitted are parts a bench strip should leave alone.
steps.quote:
IMPORTANT: Do not strip your
pistol further than previously
described.
steps.cite: COLT GOLD CUP NATIONAL MATCH MK IV/SERIES 70 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Maintenance — Stripping for Cleaning, printed p.27

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The cleaning rod is what kills a match barrel
deepSteps.action: Colt puts this in the cleaning procedure and it is the single most important sentence in it for THIS pistol: avoid contact between the cleaning rod and the muzzle, because the resulting wear will reduce accuracy. ⚠ Work from the breech, and if you must use the muzzle, use a guide.
deepSteps.prose: The crown is the last thing the bullet touches. A rod dragged across it a thousand times is a slow way to lose what you paid for.
deepSteps.quote:
Note: Avoid contact between cleaning rod and muzzle as resultant
wear will reduce accuracy.
deepSteps.cite: COLT GOLD CUP NATIONAL MATCH MK IV/SERIES 70 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Maintenance — How to Clean, printed p.29

deepSteps.title: ⚠ Brush ALL THE WAY THROUGH before reversing
deepSteps.action: If the bore is still dirty after patches, a brass bristle brush and cleaning solution. ⛔ Pass the brush ALL THE WAY THROUGH the barrel before you reverse it — Colt's own reason is that a brush reversed inside the bore will stick.
deepSteps.prose: A stuck brush in a match barrel is a genuinely bad afternoon.
deepSteps.quote:
Thoroughly scrub out barrel, passing the brush all the way
through before reversing the movement. If you try to change direction
with brush in barrel, the brush will stick.
deepSteps.cite: COLT GOLD CUP NATIONAL MATCH MK IV/SERIES 70 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Maintenance — How to Clean, step 5, printed p.29

deepSteps.title: How often, when it has NOT been fired
deepSteps.action: Colt gives an interval for a pistol that is not being shot: once or twice a year in a temperate climate, as often as once a month in a tropical one. ⚠ And if it gets wet, clean it as soon as possible regardless.
deepSteps.prose: A safe queen still corrodes. The interval is about humidity, not use.
deepSteps.aside:
If you get your pistol
wet, clean it as soon as possible.
deepSteps.quote:
When your pistol has not been fired, clean it periodically; we
suggest once or twice a year in a temperate climate, or as often as
once a month in a tropical climate.
deepSteps.cite: COLT GOLD CUP NATIONAL MATCH MK IV/SERIES 70 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Maintenance — When to Clean, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Below freezing — a DRY lubricant, not oil
deepSteps.action: Colt's note on cold weather: avoid oil for lubrication and apply a dry lubricant sparingly instead. ⚠ Oil that thickens in the cold slows a 1911's slide, and a target pistol is often shot in exactly the conditions this warns about.
deepSteps.prose: The lubricant that protects it in summer is the one that slows it in January.
deepSteps.aside: Strip for cleaning as previously described.
deepSteps.quote:
avoid the use of oil for
lubrication; instead, apply a dry lubricant sparingly.
deepSteps.cite: COLT GOLD CUP NATIONAL MATCH MK IV/SERIES 70 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Maintenance — How to Clean, printed p.29

deepSteps.title: ⚠ The trigger stop and the Eliason sight — the two adjustables
deepSteps.action: This pistol carries an ADJUSTABLE TRIGGER STOP that limits finger movement after sear release, and an adjustable square-notch Colt ELIASON rear sight with positive windage and elevation. ⛔ Both are set-and-check items, not clean-every-time items: note where they are before a strip so you can tell if handling has moved them.
deepSteps.prose: The two things on this pistol that are adjusted for the shooter are the two things worth checking after it has been apart.
deepSteps.aside:
The adjustable square notch Colt Eliason rear sight features
positive windage and elevation adjustment.
deepSteps.quote:
An adjustable trigger stop limits finger movement after sear release
so that aim is not disturbed.
deepSteps.cite: COLT GOLD CUP NATIONAL MATCH MK IV/SERIES 70 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Section 2 — Main Features, printed p.4

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Flannel patch on the rod from the BREECH, repeat until a patch comes out clean
⛔ Rod kept OFF the muzzle — that wear costs accuracy
Brass brush and solution only if the bore is still dirty after firing

cleaning.name: SLIDE AND BREECH FACE
tasks: Rear face of the barrel and the breech face brushed with a small toothbrush
Slide rails and the bushing seat wiped clean
Bushing checked for burrs — it is a fitted part on this pistol

cleaning.name: OIL
tasks: A patch lightly moistened with gun oil passed once through the bore
That film LEFT IN if the pistol is going into storage
⛔ In freezing conditions a DRY lubricant instead of oil

reassembly: Colt's own instruction: assemble in reverse order, steps 11 back through 7.
Barrel and bushing into the slide first, then the slide onto the receiver until the link shows through the slide stop hole.
Slide stop through the receiver and the barrel link — ⚠ taking care not to scratch the pistol.
Slide stop snapped home by pressing UP and IN against its detent with the disassembly notch aligned.
Then steps 5 back through 1: hammer down safely, spring and plug in, bushing turned back under pressure.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed unloaded, cycle the slide fully several times and feel it run without binding — a match bushing makes this stiffer than a service 1911 and that is normal. Check the slide stop is fully seated and its detent has sprung. Work the thumb safety and the grip safety in turn. ⚠ Then check the ADJUSTABLE TRIGGER STOP has not shifted during handling: Colt fits it so finger movement stops the instant the sear releases, and a stop that has moved either blocks the trigger or stops doing its job.
